title: Quick OCD Test
summary: Ten personal questions about intrusive thoughts, repeated routines and how much they affect your day.

landing.intro:
10 quick questions. Familiar patterns.
How many sound like you?

about.body:
This ten-question self-check asks about unwanted recurring thoughts, checking, cleaning, counting, ordering, reassurance, avoidance and daily impact. It groups your answers into a cautious pattern summary; it does not calculate whether you have OCD.

Almost everyone has unwanted thoughts or repeats an action occasionally. OCD involves obsessions, compulsions or both that are difficult to control, time-consuming, distressing or disruptive. Other experiences and conditions can look similar, so only a qualified professional can assess the full picture.

steps: Choose the answer that best matches your recent experience.
Think about frequency, distress and disruption rather than one isolated day.
Reveal your personal pattern summary after all ten questions.

about.disclaimer: For general information only. This is not a diagnostic test, validated OCD screener or substitute for professional care. It cannot confirm or rule out OCD or another condition. If thoughts or routines are distressing, time-consuming or interfering with daily life, speak with a qualified mental-health professional. Seek urgent local help if you may harm yourself or someone else.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your ten answers have been reviewed and your personal pattern summary is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: Nothing Strongly Repeated In Your Answers
profile-1.copy: Your answers did not highlight one dominant pattern of intrusive thoughts or repeated routines. That cannot rule out OCD, and a self-check cannot account for every experience. Seek professional advice if something is causing distress or disrupting daily life.

profile-2.title: Recurring Doubt Deserves Context
profile-2.copy: Your answers centred on unwanted thoughts, doubt or a sense that something is not right. Many experiences can contribute to this pattern. If the thoughts are recurring, distressing or hard to control, a qualified professional can help you understand them.

profile-3.title: The Relief Loop May Be Taking Hold
profile-3.copy: Your answers highlighted checking, repeating, cleaning, ordering or reassurance that briefly reduces discomfort. Temporary relief followed by renewed doubt can be an important pattern to discuss with a qualified mental-health professional.

profile-4.title: It May Be Time To Ask For Support
profile-4.copy: Your answers suggest that thoughts or routines may be consuming time, causing distress or limiting everyday activities. This result is not a diagnosis, but it is a reasonable prompt to arrange a professional assessment and describe how the pattern affects your life.

ocd-q1.question: How often do unwanted thoughts, images or urges return even when you try to dismiss them?

answers.a2: Occasionally, but I can move on
answers.a3: I do something repeatedly to make them go away
answers.a4: Very often, and they disrupt my day

ocd-q2.question: What happens when you are unsure whether you locked a door or completed a task correctly?

answers.a1: I usually trust myself and move on
answers.a2: The doubt lingers in my mind
answers.a3: I check or repeat the action for reassurance
answers.a4: I can lose significant time checking

ocd-q3.question: How do concerns about germs, contamination or cleanliness affect you?

answers.a3: I wash, clean or seek reassurance repeatedly
answers.a4: They make me avoid things or disrupt daily life

ocd-q4.question: How do you react when objects or actions do not feel arranged, balanced or completed in the right way?

answers.a1: I can usually leave them alone
answers.a2: It bothers me more than I expect
answers.a3: I repeat or rearrange things until they feel right
answers.a4: I struggle to continue until I correct them

ocd-q5.question: Do you count, repeat words silently or perform mental routines to reduce anxiety?

answers.a3: Yes, I repeat them for temporary relief
answers.a4: Yes, and stopping feels very difficult

ocd-q6.question: How often do you ask other people for reassurance about the same worry?

answers.a4: So often that it affects me or other people

ocd-q7.question: Do you avoid places, objects or situations because they may trigger distressing thoughts or routines?

answers.a2: Occasionally, because the thoughts are uncomfortable
answers.a3: Often, to avoid needing a ritual
answers.a4: Yes, and it limits normal activities

ocd-q8.question: After checking or completing a routine, how long does the relief usually last?

answers.a1: I do not usually need a routine
answers.a3: Relief is brief and I may repeat it
answers.a4: The doubt returns quickly and the loop consumes time

ocd-q9.question: How much control do you feel you have over these thoughts or repeated actions?

answers.a2: Some thoughts are difficult to dismiss
answers.a3: I often feel driven to complete a routine
answers.a4: Resisting causes major distress or disruption

ocd-q10.question: Which description best matches the overall effect on your life?

answers.a4: They cause substantial distress or interfere with daily life
